title: The night market
text:
Every Saturday, Aisyah goes to the night market with her father. The street is closed to cars, and hundreds of lights hang above the stalls. Today, she has ten thousand rupiah in her pocket. It is her first time to choose by herself.

She walks past stalls of toys, fried bananas and bright scarves. A man is selling tiny wooden birds that whistle when you blow into them. Aisyah wants one at once, but the price is fifteen thousand rupiah. She counts her coins again. It is not enough.

Then she smells sweet corn roasting over charcoal. The corn costs eight thousand rupiah. Aisyah smiles and buys one. It is hot, buttery and delicious.

On the way home, her father asks, "Do you wish you had the wooden bird?" Aisyah thinks for a moment. "A little," she says. "But I will save my money. Next Saturday, I will buy it." Her father nods proudly.
